Senses.Explanation: To plunge head-first into a glue pot is to turn an apparently freeing move into an entrapment of one’s own making. Chan masters use the image when a smile, question, or proposed recognition sticks the participant more firmly in the very position being tested. Chonghua Neng applies it to Kasyapa’s smile after the flower is raised. Yunwai Xingze throws it at a questioner who asks where a universal gate of liberation is released. Lingji Xingguan tells Kui’an that his opening performance has already landed head-first in the glue. An independent case collection preserves Chonghua’s same criticism of the flower case.

DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The image diagnoses the local response as entrapping; it does not say that every smile, question, or use of glue carries this force.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The sticking consequence supplies the force of the single physical image, not another sense.

ModifierControls.Finding: 刺腦 makes the entry reckless and bodily; 膠盆 makes the destination adhesive and hard to escape.
